concepts.preferred_label: Chronic Graft-Versus-Host Disease of the Eye
concepts.why: The patient presented with chronic eye symptoms, including subconjunctival fibrosis, symblepharon formation, corneal neovascularizations, and conjunctival hyperemia, which are consistent with chronic graft-versus-host disease of the eye.
The patient's symptoms, including subconjunctival fibrosis, symblepharon formation, and conjunctival hyperemia, are consistent with ocular cicatricial pemphigoid.
The patient's corneal neovascularizations and response to treatment, as shown in the images, are consistent with corneal limbal stem cell deficiency.
The patient's chronic eye symptoms and conjunctival hyperemia are consistent with Sjögren's syndrome.
The patient's symptoms, including subconjunctival fibrosis, symblepharon formation, and conjunctival hyperemia, are consistent with Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
The patient's symptoms, including subconjunctival fibrosis, symblepharon formation, and conjunctival hyperemia, are consistent with mucous membrane pemphigoid.
The patient's corneal neovascularizations and conjunctival hyperemia are consistent with trachoma.
The patient's corneal neovascularizations and conjunctival hyperemia are consistent with vernal keratoconjunctivitis.
The patient's corneal neovascularizations and conjunctival hyperemia are consistent with atopic keratoconjunctivitis.
The patient's conjunctival hyperemia is consistent with giant papillary conjunctivitis.
